newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ING sees Barings on target in three years.
newsitem.headline: ING sees Barings on target in three years.

text.p: Financial services group ING Groep NV (ING) said on Thursday it hoped Barings, the British merchant bank it bought in 1995, will reach the group's target for return on capital within three years.
Executive board chairman Aad Jacobs said that despite outside criticism of Barings' performance since the acquisition, he was satisfied.
"I'm certainly not disappointed," he said in an interview.
ING bought Barings for 1.7 billion guilders in March 1995 after the British merchant bank was brought down by losses caused by unauthorised derivatives trading in Asia.
ING has a target for Barings to reach an annual profit of 200 million guilders, or 11 percent on capital invested.
Asked when this would be achieved, Jacobs said: "Hopefully in this planning period."
ING's current three year planning is 1997-1999.
Barings results are no longer separately listed by the Dutch group, which has integrated them into those of its investment banking division, ING Barings.
"Commercially, (the acquisition) did much better than we ever expected. It gave us world-wide name recognition," he added.
"On the banking side, we are invited into deals that we could never dream of two to three years ago. We are in the premier league of banking," he said.
"We are sure that in the coming years it will deliver us the profits that we had in mind when we did the deal."
